import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.3

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. Let $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ be the group
of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers modulo $p^m$ such that
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. The group
$P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is a finite $p$-group. For which $m$ and $n$ is it regular?

Here a finite $p$-group $G$ is *regular* in the sense of P. Hall if for all $a, b \in G$ there
is an element $c$ of $\mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$, the subgroup generated by the $p$-th powers
of the elements of the derived subgroup of $\langle a, b \rangle$, with $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$.

This file states the two partial results recorded in the editors' comments:
* Merzlyakov (1964): $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is regular if $mn < p$.
* Kolesnikov (2006): $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is regular for any $m$ if $n^2 < p$.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
* Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika* **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59 (Russian)
* S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.* **47**, no. 6 (2006), 1054–1059
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«8.3»

/--
A group $G$ is *regular* in the sense of P. Hall, with respect to the prime $p$, if for all
$a, b \in G$ there is an element $c$ of the subgroup generated by the $p$-th powers of the
elements of the derived subgroup
$\langle a, b \rangle' = [\langle a, b \rangle, \langle a, b \rangle]$ of $\langle a, b \rangle$
such that $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$.

Equivalently, $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c_1^p \cdots c_k^p$ for some
$c_1, \dots, c_k \in \langle a, b \rangle'$. A finite $p$-group satisfying this condition is
called a regular $p$-group.
-/
def IsHallRegular (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : G,
    ∃ c ∈ Subgroup.closure
        {x | ∃ y ∈ ⁅Subgroup.closure {a, b}, Subgroup.closure {a, b}⁆, y ^ p = x},
      (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p * c

/-- Every abelian group is Hall-regular (take $c = 1$). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isHallRegular_of_commGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsHallRegular p G :=
  fun a b => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [mul_pow, mul_one]⟩

variable (n p m : ℕ)

/--
The multiplicative monoid of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers modulo
$p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1 \pmod p$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all
$i > j$. A congruence modulo $p$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ is expressed as divisibility by $p$.
-/
def unitriangularModSubmonoid : Submonoid (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  carrier := {A | (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧
    ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j}
  one_mem' := ⟨fun i => by simp, fun i j hij => by simp [Matrix.one_apply_ne hij.ne']⟩
  mul_mem' := by
    rintro A B ⟨hA₁, hA₂⟩ ⟨hB₁, hB₂⟩
    refine ⟨fun i => ?_, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
    · rw [Matrix.mul_apply, ← Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ i)]
      have : A i i * B i i + ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, A i k * B k i - 1 =
          (A i i - 1) * B i i + (B i i - 1) + ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, A i k * B k i := by
        ring
      rw [this]
      refine dvd_add (dvd_add ((hA₁ i).mul_right _) (hB₁ i)) (Finset.dvd_sum fun k hk => ?_)
      rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hk) with h | h
      · exact (hA₂ i k h).mul_right _
      · exact (hB₂ k i h).mul_left _
    · rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
      refine Finset.dvd_sum fun k _ => ?_
      rcases le_or_gt k j with h | h
      · exact (hA₂ i k (h.trans_lt hij)).mul_right _
      · exact (hB₂ k j h).mul_left _

/--
The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers
modulo $p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1 \pmod p$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for
all $i > j$, i.e. the matrices whose reduction modulo $p$ is upper unitriangular. It is realised
as the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$ of invertible matrices satisfying these
congruences; every such matrix is invertible, since its determinant is $\equiv 1 \pmod p$.
-/
def P [Fact p.Prime] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  toSubmonoid := (unitriangularModSubmonoid n p m).comap (Units.coeHom _)
  inv_mem' := by
    intro u hu
    have hfin : IsOfFinOrder u := isOfFinOrder_of_finite u
    have hinv : u⁻¹ ∈ Submonoid.powers u :=
      hfin.mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers.mpr ((Subgroup.zpowers u).inv_mem (Subgroup.mem_zpowers u))
    exact Submonoid.powers_le.mpr hu hinv

/-- An invertible matrix $u$ lies in $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ iff $u_{ii} \equiv 1 \pmod p$ for
all $i$ and $u_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_P_iff [Fact p.Prime] (u : GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    u ∈ P n p m ↔
      (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (u : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i i - 1) ∧
        ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (u : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i j :=
  Iff.rfl

/--
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is
regular if $mn < p$ (Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika* **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.3».variants.merzlyakov_1964 [Fact p.Prime] (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n)
    (h : m * n < p) : IsHallRegular p (P n p m) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is
regular for any $m$ if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.* **47**, no. 6 (2006),
1054–1059).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.3».variants.kolesnikov_2006 [Fact p.Prime] (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n)
    (h : n ^ 2 < p) : IsHallRegular p (P n p m) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.3»

modeling_decisions: The condition '$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$' is read as a congruence modulo $p$ (the trailing '(mod p)' in the source qualifies both congruences). This is the only reading under which the set is a group for $m \ge 2$: with $a_{ii} = 1$ exactly in $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$, e.g. $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\p&1\end{pmatrix}$ has $A^2$ with diagonal $1+p \ne 1$ mod $p^2$. It also matches the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$ studied in the cited Merzlyakov/Kolesnikov papers.
Congruence modulo $p$ inside `ZMod (p ^ m)` is expressed as divisibility `(p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ ·`, which avoids needing `m ≠ 0` for a `ZMod.castHom` to `ZMod p`.

$P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is realised as a subgroup of `GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))`, i.e. as the *units* whose matrix satisfies the congruences. Every matrix satisfying the congruences is automatically invertible (its determinant is ≡ 1 mod p, hence a unit of Z/p^m), so this is the same group as the set of matrices in the source.

The definition `P` carries a `[Fact p.Prime]` instance argument; it is used only to obtain finiteness of GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m)) for the inverse-closure proof. The source assumes p prime throughout, and both theorems assume it anyway.

Hall-regularity is defined for an arbitrary group with a parameter p (not restricted to finite p-groups); the source's group is a finite p-group and the theorems apply the definition with the same prime p. The element c is taken in `Subgroup.closure` of the set of p-th powers of the derived subgroup ⁅⟨a,b⟩,⟨a,b⟩⁆ — equivalent to Hall's original product $c_1^p\cdots c_k^p$ formulation.

Hypotheses `0 < m` and `0 < n` are included in both theorems to reflect 'positive integers' in the source setup (for Kolesnikov, 'for any m' is read as any positive integer m). Bounds `m * n < p` and `n ^ 2 < p` are strict as in the source.
The open question 'For which m and n is it regular?' and the Yagzhev (m = 1) / Kolesnikov 2001 (m = 2) remarks are not formalized, per the decomposition table.

$P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ consists of the invertible $n \times n$ matrices whose
reduction modulo $p$ is upper unitriangular. Problem 8.3 asks for which $m$ and
$n$ this finite $p$-group is regular in the sense of Hall.

The declarations below record two known sufficient conditions from the
editors' comments: $mn<p$, due to Merzlyakov, and the bound $n^2<p$, independent
of $m$, due to Kolesnikov.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.3»

/--
The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$. Its matrices reduce modulo $p$ to upper
unitriangular matrices: each diagonal entry is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, and
each entry strictly below the diagonal is congruent to $0$ modulo $p$.
-/
def P (p m n : ℕ) : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :=
  Subgroup.closure {A | (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧
    ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j}

/--
A group is Hall-regular at $p$ if, for every $x,y$, the discrepancy between
$(xy)^p$ and $x^p y^p$ is a product of $p$-th powers of elements of the
derived subgroup of $\langle x,y\rangle$.
-/
def IsHallRegular (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G,
    let H : Subgroup G := Subgroup.closure {x, y}
    ∃ cs : List G, (∀ c ∈ cs, c ∈ ⁅H, H⁆) ∧
      (x * y) ^ p = x ^ p * y ^ p * (cs.map fun c ↦ c ^ p).prod

/--
Merzlyakov's 1964 result: if $p$ is prime, $m,n$ are positive, and $mn<p$,
then $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is a regular $p$-group in Hall's sense.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem variants.merzlyakov_1964 :
    ∀ (p m n : ℕ), p.Prime → 0 < m → 0 < n → m * n < p →
      IsHallRegular p (P p m n) := by
  sorry

/--
Kolesnikov's 2006 result: if $p$ is prime and $n$ is positive with $n^2<p$,
then, for every positive $m$, $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is a regular $p$-group
in Hall's sense. In particular, this bound is independent of $m$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem variants.kolesnikov_2006 :
    ∀ (p n : ℕ), p.Prime → 0 < n → n ^ 2 < p →
      ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < m → IsHallRegular p (P p m n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.3»
modeling_decisions: Modeled P_n(ZMod (p^m)) as the subgroup closure in GL_n(ZMod (p^m)) of the matrices whose diagonal entries are congruent to 1 modulo p and whose strictly lower entries are congruent to 0 modulo p. The generating set is mathematically already a subgroup, and all matrices satisfying these reduction conditions are invertible for the positive prime-power moduli in the theorem.

Read the displayed '(mod p)' as governing both the diagonal congruence to 1 and the strictly lower congruence to 0. Reading the diagonal condition as literal equality in ZMod (p^m) would not define a group under matrix multiplication.

Defined Hall regularity using the standard identity (xy)^p = x^p y^p c_1^p ... c_k^p, where each correction element lies in the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by x and y. A List represents the finite ordered product.

Kept positivity hypotheses on both m and n in both variants. This excludes ZMod 0 and faithfully reflects that m and n are positive integers; Kolesnikov's quantifier over m is placed after the n^2 < p bound to emphasize that the bound is independent of m.

/-!

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. Let $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ be the
group of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers modulo $p^m$ such that
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. The group

*Editors' comment (2001):* The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is known to be regular if
$mn < p$ (Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika*, **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59 (Russian)).
The case $m = 1$ is completely done by A. V. Yagzhev in (*Math. Notes*, **56**, no. 5–6
(1995), 1283–1290), although this paper is erroneous for $m > 1$. The case $m = 2$ is
completed in (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Issledovaniya in analysis and algebra*, no. 3, Tomsk Univ.,
Tomsk, 2001, 117–125 (Russian)).

*Editors' comment (2009):* The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ was shown to be regular for
any $m$ if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.*, **47**, no. 6 (2006),
1054–1059).

Here a finite $p$-group $G$ is *regular* in the sense of P. Hall if for all $x, y \in G$
there is $c \in ℧_1(\langle x, y \rangle')$ with $(xy)^p = x^p y^p c$, where
$\langle x, y \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by $x$ and $y$,
and $℧_1(H)$ denotes the subgroup generated by the $p$-th powers of the elements of $H$.

Both congruences in the definition of $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ are modulo $p$: it is the
group of matrices over $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ whose reduction modulo $p$ is upper unitriangular,
i.e. the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. Every such matrix is
invertible (its determinant is $\equiv 1 \pmod p$), so $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is
formalised as a subgroup of `GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))`.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 8.3
- Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika* **3** (1964), no. 4, 49–59
- S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.* **47** (2006), no. 6, 1054–1059
- P. Hall, *A contribution to the theory of groups of prime power order*,
  Proc. London Math. Soc. (2) **36** (1934), 29–95
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«8.3»

/--
A group $G$ is a *regular $p$-group* in the sense of P. Hall if it is a $p$-group and for
all $x, y \in G$ there is an element $c$ of $℧_1(\langle x, y \rangle')$ with
$(xy)^p = x^p y^p c$. Here $\langle x, y \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup
$\langle x, y \rangle$ generated by $x$ and $y$, and $℧_1(H)$ is the subgroup generated by
the $p$-th powers of the elements of $H$.

Equivalently, $(xy)^p = x^p y^p s_1^p \cdots s_k^p$ for some
$s_1, \dots, s_k \in \langle x, y \rangle'$, which is Hall's original formulation.
-/
def IsRegularPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ x y : G,
    ∃ c ∈ Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) ''
      ((⁅Subgroup.closure {x, y}, Subgroup.closure {x, y}⁆ : Subgroup G) : Set G)),
      (x * y) ^ p = x ^ p * y ^ p * c

/-- Every abelian $p$-group is regular. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsRegularPGroup.of_commGroup {p : ℕ} {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    IsRegularPGroup p G :=
  ⟨hG, fun x y => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [mul_pow, mul_one]⟩⟩

section Unitriangular

variable (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [LinearOrder ι] (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

/-- The diagonal entries of a product of two upper triangular matrices are the products of
the corresponding diagonal entries. -/
private lemma mul_apply_self_of_blockTriangular {A B : Matrix ι ι R} (hA : A.BlockTriangular id)
    (hB : B.BlockTriangular id) (i : ι) : (A * B) i i = A i i * B i i := by
  rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
  refine Finset.sum_eq_single i (fun k _ hk => ?_) (by simp)
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hk with h | h
  · rw [hA (show id k < id i from h), zero_mul]

A finite $p$-group $G$ is *regular* (P. Hall) if for all $a, b \in G$ there is
$c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ with $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$, where $\langle a, b \rangle'$
is the derived subgroup of $\langle a, b \rangle$ and $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$.

Editors' comment (2001): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is known to be regular if $mn < p$
(Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika*, **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59 (Russian)). The case $m = 1$
is completely done by A. V. Yagzhev in (*Math. Notes*, **56**, no. 5–6 (1995), 1283–1290),
although this paper is erroneous for $m > 1$. The case $m = 2$ is completed in
(S. G. Kolesnikov, *Issledovaniya in analysis and algebra*, no. 3, Tomsk Univ., Tomsk, 2001,
117–125 (Russian)).

Editors' comment (2009): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ was shown to be regular for any $m$
if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.*, **47**, no. 6 (2006), 1054–1059).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

section RegularPGroup

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The subgroup $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$ of $G$ generated by the $p$-th
powers of the elements of a subgroup $H$. -/
def agemo (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) '' (H : Set G))

/-- A group $G$ is a *regular $p$-group* in the sense of P. Hall if it is a $p$-group and for
all $a, b \in G$ there is $c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ such that $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$,
where $\langle a, b \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by $a$ and $b$. -/
def IsRegularPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ a b : G,
    ∃ c ∈ agemo p ⁅Subgroup.closure {a, b}, Subgroup.closure {a, b}⁆,
      (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p * c

/-- Every abelian $p$-group is regular: one can take $c = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPGroup.isRegularPGroup_of_isMulCommutative {p : ℕ} [IsMulCommutative G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p G) : IsRegularPGroup p G :=
  ⟨hG, fun a b => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [(Commute.all a b).mul_pow, mul_one]⟩⟩

end RegularPGroup

section MatrixGroup

variable {n p m : ℕ}

/-- A matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ is *unitriangular modulo $p$* if $a_{ii} \equiv 1$
for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
def IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧ ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j

private lemma isUnitriangularModP_iff (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    IsUnitriangularModP A ↔ ∀ i j, j ≤ i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A - 1) i j := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hd, hl⟩ i j hij
    rcases hij.lt_or_eq with h | h
    · simpa [Matrix.one_apply, h.ne'] using hl i j h
    · subst h
      simpa using hd _
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun i => by simpa using h i i le_rfl, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
    simpa [Matrix.one_apply, hij.ne'] using h i j hij.le

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.one :
    IsUnitriangularModP (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff]
  simp

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.mul {A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (hB : IsUnitriangularModP B) :
    IsUnitriangularModP (A * B) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff] at hA hB ⊢
  intro i j hij
  have : A * B - 1 = (A - 1) + (B - 1) + (A - 1) * (B - 1) := by noncomm_ring
  rw [this, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
  refine dvd_add (dvd_add (hA i j hij) (hB i j hij)) (Finset.dvd_sum fun k _ => ?_)
  by_cases hk : k ≤ i
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left (hA i k hk) _
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hB k j (hij.trans (not_le.mp hk).le)) _

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.pow {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (k : ℕ) : IsUnitriangularModP (A ^ k) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => exact IsUnitriangularModP.one
  | succ k ih => exact pow_succ A k ▸ ih.mul hA

variable (n p m) in
/-- The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers
modulo $p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all
$i > j$, as a subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. -/
def P [Fact p.Prime] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  carrier := {A | IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m)))}
  one_mem' := IsUnitriangularModP.one
  mul_mem' hA hB := hA.mul hB
  inv_mem' {A} hA := by
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := (isOfFinOrder_of_finite A).mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers.mpr
      (Subgroup.inv_mem _ (Subgroup.mem_zpowers A))
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← hk]
    exact hA.pow k

/-- Membership in `P n p m` unfolds to the defining congruences: `A ∈ P n p m` if and only if
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_P_iff [Fact p.Prime] (A : GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    A ∈ P n p m ↔
      (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i i - 1) ∧
        ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i j :=
  Iff.rfl

end MatrixGroup

attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The two editors'-comment results are the only statable propositions; the main question ('for which m and n') and the Yagzhev/Kolesnikov-2001 case remarks have no statable Prop, as the table says.
modeling_decisions: Reading of the diagonal condition: the notebook writes 'a_ii ≡ 1 for all i and a_ij ≡ 0 (mod p) for all i > j'. I read BOTH congruences modulo p (P_n is the preimage of the upper unitriangular group under reduction mod p, i.e. a Sylow p-subgroup of GL_n(Z/p^m)). The alternative reading a_ii = 1 exactly in Z/p^m does not define a group when m, n ≥ 2 (e.g. [[1,1],[p,1]]^2 has (1,1)-entry 1+p over Z/p^2), so it cannot be intended. This is noted in the module docstring.
Congruence 'x ≡ 0 (mod p)' for x ∈ ZMod (p^m) is encoded as divisibility (p : ZMod (p^m)) ∣ x, which is equivalent for m ≥ 1 and avoids a side condition m ≠ 0 that ZMod.castHom would need.

IsRegularPGroup p G includes the conjunct IsPGroup p G (so it literally means 'G is a regular p-group'); the source itself asserts P_n(Z_{p^m}) is a finite p-group, so this adds no false claim. Hall's condition is stated with c ∈ ℧₁(⟨a,b⟩') and (ab)^p = a^p b^p c (equivalent to the product-of-p-th-powers form since ℧₁ is generated by p-th powers).

P n p m carries a [Fact p.Prime] instance argument; it is only used to obtain finiteness of GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p^m)) for the proof of inv_mem'. The slot theorems use the same [Fact p.Prime] hypothesis for 'p a prime'.
The positivity hypotheses 0 < m and 0 < n are kept as in the source ('positive integers') although they are mathematically inessential for the truth of the statements.
Two fully proved @[category API] lemmas were added as sanity tests of the bespoke definitions (mem_P_iff unfolding the defining congruences, and abelian p-groups are regular). They are not slots.
